description: Aurorasaurus collects auroral sightings reported by the public on its website, and its open database is especially rich during strong geomagnetic storms, when crowdsourced reports show how far towards the equator the aurora, and so the disturbance, reached. The Zenodo release by Elizabeth MacDonald, the New Mexico Consortium, Laura Brandt Edson and Feras Natsheh holds web observations from August 2014 to August 2025 as cleaned and transformed CSV files (about 8 MB each), described in a technical report submitted to Frontiers in Astronomy and Space Sciences on crowdsourced observations during geomagnetic superstorms, with a companion notebook and an earlier 2018 real-time data release. Version 1.0 was published on 16 May 2026 and is accessible as a free download from Zenodo under CC BY-NC 4.0. Caveats: sightings are volunteered, depend on weather, darkness and where people live, and are not a calibrated measurement. It supports reconstruction of the extent of geomagnetic storms that drive induced currents in power grids and pipelines, as crowdsourced evidence alongside magnetometer data; related records are SuperMAG, INTERMAGNET and the GFZ Kp index.
